- **The `reachy` capability — jarvis S3: memory semantics and a durable, exact-id OrgEvent audit on a stub sidecar.** The office agent's body (`src/capabilities/reachy/`) registers four tools and consumes the sidecar's JSON lines, decoded against a STRICT schema before policy (every wire type, outer envelope included, has `additionalProperties: false`; a malformed line — unknown field, bad shape, or an oversized line is a `reachy.malformed` OrgEvent, never a throw; the 64 KiB bound is counted in UTF-8 BYTES and discards an oversized line THROUGH its newline, so a multi-byte transcript over the bound in bytes is refused and a payload on the same line cannot slip through). Authority stays in bob: a transcript is written as a `private` memory authored by `jarvis` with the speakerId only when addressed and speakerVerified (bob's enrolment, EMPTY in v1), and its audit event — the SAME record shape the observatory emits — is persisted FIRST as an ATTEMPT with a record id, and the memory then carries the id of the OUTCOME event — the `written` event, NEVER the attempt. SUCCESS is returned only when the `written` event is persisted under that EXACT pre-generated id AND read back as the `written` outcome whose targetIds contain this memory (when the store reports an id it must equal the pre-generated one; a store that reports none is accepted on readback); if the memory exists and its `written` audit failed — a thrown write, a mismatched id, or a null readback — the outcome is a linked `failed` and an UNAUDITED refusal, and the memory is retained; a refusal does NOT assert that no written event targeting it exists — the query explains a memory when the `written` id in its metadata resolves to a `written` event whose `targetIds` contain that memory (an exact-id read, not a search) (a store that persists the `written` event and then throws is refused yet still explains the memory); a failed write is never an unqualified "wrote"; otherwise "why do you know this" reads the `written` event back by exact id across a restart. Proposal arguments are validated BY ACTION before policy (typed, BOUNDED `look` yaw/pitch — yaw in [-180,180], pitch in [-90,90] — and a one-line speech text: at most 500 chars, no CR/LF; `additionalProperties: false` everywhere — an out-of-range yaw, a multi-line or oversized speech line, a string yaw or an extra field is `reachy.malformed` and is never sent), and the speech gate applies to `ask` (which IS speech): an `ask` carrying a memory input is refused, never sent as a `say`. The visitor acknowledgement rate slot is reserved synchronously before the audit (and rolled back if the audit fails), so concurrent visitor lines cannot both acknowledge. Record ids are unique ACROSS processes — the memory id `<agentId>-<random UUID>`, the event id `evt_<kind>_<random UUID>`, the
  OrgEvent record id is `orgevent-<event id>`, so two bob processes with one agentId never collide. The actuation tools (`reachy_look`/`reachy_say`/`reachy_frame`) and proposals go through the same admit path (mute, rate gate, one OrgEvent per command; `frame` sends a `frame` command); the registered tool parameter schemas ARE the per-action runtime schemas (`ACTION_ARG_SCHEMAS.look`/`.say`), so `reachy_look` advertises and enforces yaw [-180,180] and pitch [-90,90], and `reachy_say` a one-line text of at most 500 chars — pi never advertises an input the runtime rejects as malformed; `reachy_say` accepts NO memory reference: the tool's schema rejects an extra argument BEFORE execute (pi validates first), and a direct caller of execute still gets an audited `reachy.refused`; `answer` is OFF and `reachy_state` is declared a PLACEHOLDER that sends an ungated `state` request (no request/response correlation yet). The replay proof pins its expected count and outcomes as CONSTANTS independent of the fixture (a truncated replay fails) and waits for the stub's explicit end-of-replay marker; the key-read proof makes the fixture dir traversable and shows a DIFFERENT OS user can read a 0644 control file but NOT the 0600 key fixtures. (`test/capabilities/reachy/`, `test/capabilities/flair/capability.test.ts`)
